newsitem.title: FRANCE: French women unimpressed by Juppe's campaign-poll.
newsitem.headline: French women unimpressed by Juppe's campaign-poll.

text.p: French women are not impressed by a seduction campaign by Prime Minister Alain Juppe, according to an opinion poll on Tuesday which places him only eighth among politicians seen by women as an "ideal prime minister".
The BVA survey, to be published in the weekly magazine Paris Match, showed that just 11 percent of French women saw conservative Juppe as the ideal person for the post.

Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin topped the poll with 23 percent, ahead of former conservative prime minister Edouard Balladur on 22 percent and rising Socialist star Martine Aubry, daughter of former European Commission head Jacques Delors, with 20 percent.
The women polled were allowed three choices.

Juppe's December campaign, aimed at the public at large but primarily directed at women, included a book he wrote revealing his "inner self" and interviews given to the women's monthly Elle and to Paris Match which has a strong feminine readership.
The campaign was aimed at countering a largely held public view that Juppe is a cold technocrat who haughtily dismisses the everyday concerns of French families.
Juppe said he felt moved to write the book after a woman he passed on a street insulted him.
Recurrent public opinion polls show Juppe is the country's least popular prime minister in decades.
The poll was held between December 27 and January 4. It was conducted by the BVA group among 993 women.
